music.selection_method: MASTER_PLAN 6.1: shortlist from the cached Mixkit catalogue (281 tracks parsed from 18 category pages saved 2026-10-22; no new catalogue requests), Pebble-profile ranking from tags and public waveform envelopes (tools/audio/mixkit_rank_pebble.py), then a no-ears audition of the top 5 (analyze_track.py PNGs, all looked at; Apple SoundAnalysis via sound_tags; rubric_metrics.py), scored with tools/audio/score_rubric.py and tools/audio/rubric_judgments.json.

music.decision: No Mixkit candidate reached 70/100: the top stock score is 67 (431), which also fails the small-speaker gate like 282 (66); the best eligible track is 79 at 64. So the MASTER_PLAN 6.2 gate sends the film to the composed fallback. B1 (huashu-motion composer mode with its CC0 sample pack) could not be run: the session's permission system blocked executing that downloaded third-party CLI, so B2 was used: an original score rendered by our own code (tools/audio/compose_score.py, numpy + scipy + pedalboard), no samples and no third-party music. B1 stays available if the user approves running huashu-motion (pinned commit 52467f99c602b76ba86d511d37acdfe93fa1e16e). UPDATE 2026-10-23 (HANDOFF-C2): the user asked for a professional score, so the same composition is now played on recorded CC0 instrument samples (VCSL, VSCO 2 CE) by our own sampler (tools/audio/render_sampled.py; no downloaded code was run). The sampled bed passes every gate (beat grid, reveal, length; H9 small-speaker share and mono fold-down; SoundAnalysis; web and social loudness) and scores 93/100 against 91 for the synthesised original, so it is the default; the grid is identical, so no picture changes. The synthesised original stays one command away (tools/audio/use_music.sh original).

opening.why: A feed starts the film from silence. Heard that way, the score's first notes on the recorded marimba read as a ringtone in Apple SoundAnalysis (one 3 s window: silence, then the film's first 0.75 s or 1.5 s).
what: bar 1's motif (D-A-G#-A) an octave lower, on the upright piano (VCSL) in its soft layer: a warm attack with a full row of harmonics, where the marimba gave a bare fundamental and a bright 4th partial
legato: the D rings 1.4 s under the phrase; the A-G#-A turn passes from key to key with 60 ms dampers, so the semitone does not beat on like a phone's warble
the strings' D(add9) (the score's own bar-1 pad, viola section) enter with it on the downbeat with the score's 0.9 s swell, so the motif never sounds alone after silence
bar 2's answer stays on the marimba as written; bars 8, 23 and 29 (the motif's returns) are unchanged
each re-voiced note stays in the event list, muted: it still draws its random numbers and calibrates its bus, so everything after bar 1 plays exactly as in lane C2's bed

what: VCSL Marimba (Outrigger mallets), 3 dynamics: soft, med, loud
VCSL Vibraphone, soft mallets, 2 dynamics (v1, v2), motor off
VCSL Upright Piano (Yamaha, 'Upright No. 1' cleaned and remastered), sustain pedal off, 2 dynamics (vl1 with 2 round robins, vl2)
VSCO 2 CE Viola Section, sustain with vibrato, 2 dynamics (v1, v2): the pad's lower voices (up to D4)
VSCO 2 CE Violin Section, sustain with vibrato, 2 dynamics (v1, v2): the pad's upper voices (E4 and up)
VSCO 2 CE Solo Contrabass pizzicato, 2 dynamics where recorded (v1, v3), 2 round robins
VCSL Bass Drum 1, 4 dynamics (v2, v3, v5, v7), 2 round robins
VCSL small shaker, down and up strokes, 2 round robins

mapping_notes: the score's kalimba part is played on the upright piano: the recorded kalimba (VCSL, Tanzania) was tried first; SoundAnalysis heard its tines as cowbell (0.49), bell (0.63), ringtone (0.40) and telephone (0.36), so it was dropped
the pad is the viola section; the violin section plays its upper octave (B4 and up); violins on the pad's top voices were tried and made the opening read as a telephone (0.25)

two bass-drum and two shaker candidates were compared by envelope and spectrum; VCSL Bass Drum 1 (deeper, cleaner, closest to the original felt kick) and the VCSL small shaker (down/up strokes with round robins) were kept

method.pitch: nearest sampled note in the velocity layer, pitch-shifted with soxr (VHQ resampling) from the sample's measured pitch (libraries name middle C 'C3': sounding = name + 12 semitones, measured on every file; median |offset| from the name 2.0 cents, max 34.2); max shift per part (semitones): {'mallet': 3.046, 'vibes': 2.0, 'kal': 2.981, 'glock': 1.879, 'pad': 2.036, 'bass': 2.047, 'kick': 0.0, 'perc': 0.0}
method.layers_round_robins: velocity layers and round robins where recorded; elsewhere +-3 cents and +-0.4 dB per hit
method.timing: samples trimmed to their measured onset (0.5 ms pre-roll; one bass take, BKCtbss_Pizz_G0_v3_rr2, opens with 17 ms of handling noise and has its onset set by hand); the shaker's stroke peak lands 4 ms after the note
method.transients: bass drum and pizzicato through a transient shaper (attack +5 / +4 dB; the 20-60 ms bloom of their low end held at the attack's level) so their thump peaks on the hit; without it the validator read the low end 10-30 ms late
method.tails: vibraphone pedal-up after the written hold with the score's 3.2 Hz motor; bass hand-damped after its written length; piano keys released after 1.4 s; string swell and release as written
method.mix: bus levels calibrated to the original score's measured stem loudness, then offsets (dB) {'mallet': -1.5, 'bass': 0.0, 'vibes': 0.0, 'kick': 2.0, 'kal': 3.0, 'pad': 0.5, 'glock': 0.0, 'perc': 0.0}; per-part EQ; the bass low-passed at 3 kHz (4th order); a convolution hall from an impulse response synthesised in render_sampled.py (no third-party IR); the score's fader ride; two final-bar touches (the marimba roll 6 dB softer and the strings' final chord 3 dB softer: on recorded instruments the roll under the strings read as 'foghorn' 0.6-0.9); light bus compression (1.6:1) and a brick-wall limiter 13 dB above the loudness (it never engages on this mix); normalised to -18 LUFS like compose_score.py

judge.method: both candidates' film stems as their composers delivered them (A: tools/audio/scores/trailer_a.py at 4fb110b; B: trailer_b.py at 58ba6c4), each mixed with the picture's final cue list (tools/audio/cues.json: 41 effects, 7 automation spans) at -16 LUFS by mix_master.py, then measured with the same scripts: the loudness curve by movement, the dead stop and the drop, onset density and groove (spectral-flux onsets on the score, the drive's grid alignment and pulse), brightness and the power shares, the same mix through a small-speaker band (150 Hz-12 kHz), the classifier (mix_checks.py and the trailer's after-silence passes), and the score's accents against every cue. classifier_with_the_final_cues.note: mix_checks.py's gates as they stood before its trailer windows (its 3 s windows on both grids and the opening; no fails for either), plus the judge's own after-silence passes at f0, f648, f1512 and f1656 and its readings in the trailer's windows (both holds, the push, the end card)

why: Energy, the person's ask (frontier-lab launches; the research: energy from groove, double time and hits): B's drums and bass sit 4.3 LU over its music in the montage (A: 2.1 under), and through a small-speaker band B's drums stay level with its music (-0.9 LU) where A's fall 7.5 LU under its synths.
Promise: B's hook, the motif, runs through the whole proof section; A's montage has no melody until bar 18's arp.
OVERRIDES §41: B already built the two-moment climax (the tests pass on Gmaj9 at f1656, the climb, D on the push at f1723.5); A peaks at f1656 and sat 0.8 LU under it at f1723.
Sync: B lands a score accent within a frame of 25 of the cue list's 41 effects (A: 16); its montage cuts jump 7-9 dB (A: 4-6).
against_B_and_what_was_done: Its question hits were 3.5-6 dB softer than A's; with the timeline's suck-back at -16 dB its Q1 cleared the 0.6 s before it by 7.3 dB (gate 10): the hits were raised (now 10.8 / 13.4 / 22.2 dB).

A hits harder and brighter on a phone: A's drop lands 3.3 dB louder in the small-speaker band, and A keeps 55 % of its power above 150 Hz against B's 35 % (both over the 30 % gate). Not changed: it is B's sound.
Its LRA is about 11 LU, against the 8-10 LU target (A: 11.5); a target, not a gate.
